Synopsis:
Ukrainian strikes on Russian Black Sea grain infrastructure are disrupting exports during peak season, forcing cargo delays and cancellations. The Kremlin asserts mitigation measures are in place, with Putin estimating ~60Mt available for export. Near-term export volumes are expected to recover slightly (1.95Mt in July → 2.2Mt in August per Sovecon), but supply tightness remains a live risk for global wheat importers.
